summary: Slice 03 landed on feat/03-access-entitlement-gate in three atomic commits. Baseline access is now the required boolean entitlements.access, decided by classifyHubAccess, which fails closed on ===true. The 402 wire body flipped to no_org_access. The 403 half gained a web owner: isForbiddenFailure, ForbiddenPanel and a four-arm classification chain in SalesOpsApp plus the same arm in CadastroHistoryPanel. CLAUDE.md records the access gate, the exhaustive 401/402/403/503 taxonomy including 401 contract_version_mismatch, the dated one-wave internal disagreement, and slice 02's carried explicit-Hub-configuration bullet with its Environments table and dotenv edits. No SDK version was touched; the local gate is labelled a deliberate one-wave bridge that slice 04 deletes.

already_done_steps: Step 6 - apps/web/src/lib/api-client.ts: ApiError already carries `code`, set from body.code in both apiFetch and apiFetchBlob. No edit, file not in files_modified.

Step 7 partial - isEntitlementFailure already exists in require-token.ts, keys on status === 402 alone, and is pinned by `isEntitlementFailure is true for a 402 that carries no code at all`. Left byte-unchanged including its now-stale missing_entitlement prose, which slice 04 owns.

Step 8c partial - MissingEntitlementPanel, missing-entitlement-copy.ts and the entitlement-first arm of the SalesOpsApp isError chain already shipped in v2.8.0. Only one new ternary arm, two imports and one extended comment were added.

Step 9b - entitlement-dead-end.test.tsx already existed with its four arms. Extended in place; no existing it block was touched beyond adding forbiddenPanel() null assertions to the 402, 500 and 401 arms.
Step 2 - coreModuleFromAudience was still present after slice 02, exactly as slice 02 promised, so step 2 was NOT skipped and was executed in full.
deviations_from_plan: Grep gate 2 as literally written in the plan's Verification section does not pass, because the plan's own step 3 requires `expect(config).not.toHaveProperty('coreModule')` in auth-provider.test.ts. The assertion was kept, since deleting it would delete the only pin on the deletion (toMatchObject ignores extra keys), and gate 2 was read with the same `':!*__tests__*'` pathspec that decision D6 applies to gate 1 for exactly the same reason. Gate 2 so narrowed prints nothing. Flagged for the verifier rather than resolved unilaterally in the plan.

Two CLAUDE.md lines outside the plan's named anchors were corrected because they now contradicted shipped behaviour: line 6 said `The product audience is product.fxl-sales`, which slice 02's boot check REFUSES (its `refuses to boot on a product. audience` test), and the session-store bullet said the encryption key derives from `FXL_HUB_SECRET_KEY`, a variable slice 02 retired. Both are one-word corrections inside sections this wave already edits. The `VITE_FXL_HUB_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` line in the web dotenv block was deliberately LEFT ALONE, because decision D4 assigns the VITE_ variables to slice 04.

app-auth-access-gate.test.ts declares `type MinimalHubAuthContext = import('../app-auth.js').MinimalHubAuthContext;` rather than a static type import, so the type is erased and cannot pull the module in ahead of the vi.doMock. Same effect as the plan's shape.
concerns: The integration suite emitted one INTERMITTENT unhandled rejection on the first of four runs: `PostgresError: canceling statement due to user request (57014)` on `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY sales_ops_sale_professionals_org_sale_id_id_idx`, attributed to `test/rls/professional-payable-migration.integration.test.ts > recovers an interrupted invalid concurrent index and serializes two runners`. All 169 tests passed on every run and three subsequent full runs were clean, including the recorded one. That test DELIBERATELY cancels a concurrent index build, so the escaping rejection is inherent to its own design and pre-existing: this slice touches no migration, database, connection or RLS code, and the file in isolation passes with no unhandled error. Filed rather than fixed, because closing it means editing a migration test outside this slice's declared sixteen files.

CLAUDE.md now disagrees with itself for one wave by design: the Auth Model taxonomy says the 402 code is `no_org_access` while the Organization context section still says `missing_entitlement`. That is dated in place in the file itself and is slice 04's to close under decision D2. The same staleness exists in the web tree's `missing_entitlement` literals and titles, deliberately untouched for the same reason.

`requireHubModule` is exported and tested but mounted on no route, exactly as the plan intends. It is labelled bridge coverage in a header comment above its describe block so slice 04's deletion needs no further argument.
